subsystems.name: Rectenna
subsystems.role: catches ambient radio waves and turns their alternating current into direct current.

subsystems.name: Thermoelectric layer
subsystems.role: converts a temperature difference between the skin or a warm surface and the cooler air into a small voltage.
parts: thermal insulation on the cold side

subsystems.name: Power management
subsystems.role: makes usable power from inputs of microwatts, which ordinary circuits cannot start on.

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: buffers trickles of energy so the radio can transmit in short bursts.

subsystems.name: Flexible substrate and encapsulation
subsystems.role: holds the layers together and keeps them working against sweat, bending and washing.

buildSteps.title: Choose the harvest targets
buildSteps.detail: The design is matched to whatever is actually present: common mobile and Wi-Fi bands, or a body-to-air temperature difference of a few kelvin.

buildSteps.title: Print the antenna
buildSteps.detail: Conductive silver or copper ink is screen-printed onto a flexible polymer film and cured, so the antenna bends without cracking.

buildSteps.title: Build the rectifier
buildSteps.detail: A Schottky diode and matching network are tuned so that even a few microwatts at the antenna produce a usable DC voltage.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the thermoelectric legs
buildSteps.detail: Bismuth telluride or printed thermoelectric inks are patterned into many tiny p-n couples connected in series on a flexible sheet.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power management
buildSteps.detail: A cold-start boost converter and storage capacitor are mounted as bare dies to keep the package thin.

buildSteps.title: Laminate the patch
buildSteps.detail: Layers are stacked and sealed so the hot side faces the source of heat and the cold side faces still air, maximising the gradient.

buildSteps.title: Characterise and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Each patch is tested under realistic light, RF and thermal conditions to map its output and set the duty cycle.

buildSteps.title: Pair with a radio
buildSteps.detail: The firmware is set to sense and transmit in bursts only when the storage has enough charge, then sleep.

prerequisites.why: usable power needs input densities well above typical ambient levels, so it works only near transmitters or in strong signal areas.
printed and thin-film thermoelectrics exist but produce only tens of microwatts per square centimetre from body heat.
standards such as Bluetooth Low Energy and LoRa let a sensor work on average power in the microwatt range.
they let a circuit begin boosting from a few tens of millivolts.
solid-state cells and supercapacitors are small and safe but store limited energy per unit area.

pathway.milestone: harvesting-powered sensors in industrial monitoring and building controls
pathway.unlocks: maintenance-free sensors where wiring or battery changes are impractical.

pathway.milestone: patches that run a low-rate radio purely from light, vibration or a temperature difference
pathway.unlocks: stick-on sensing on machinery and infrastructure with no batteries to replace.

pathway.milestone: combined harvesters that sum several sources on one flexible film
pathway.unlocks: more reliable output, since no single ambient source is always available.

pathway.milestone: dense ambient RF harvesting near transmitters
pathway.unlocks: battery-free tags and sensors wherever deliberate power beaming is allowed — though physics caps this at small distances and low power.
